knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=The input dataset, which can be a data.frame, MPdata, or GRanges object ;; pval.colname=The name of the column containing p-values ;; chr.colname=The name of the column containing chromosome identifiers ;; pos.colname=The name of the column containing genomic positions ;; rescale=Logical indicating whether to visually rescale the y-axis to handle highly significant p-values ;; label.colname=The name of the column containing text labels for annotation ;; highlight.colname=The name of the column used to categorize points for custom coloring ;; highlight.col=A named character vector mapping categories in highlight.colname to specific colors ;; color.by.highlight=Logical indicating whether to color points based on the highlight column ;; chromosome=An integer or character specifying a single chromosome to zoom into ;; bins.x=The number of horizontal bins for the widest chromosome in binned plots ;; bins.y=The number of vertical bins for binned plots ;; bin.palette=The palette name from the paletteer package used to color bins ;; summarise.expression.list=A list of formulas defining custom summary statistics for binned data ;; annot.method=The method used to match variants in GDS annotation (e.g., "position" or "id")
- alternatives: None mentioned.
- when_to_use: Use when visualizing genomic association study (GWAS/PWAS) results to identify significant loci, especially when highly significant p-values compress the visual scale of less significant points, or when the dataset is too large to plot individual points efficiently.
- pitfalls: Attempting to label all points instead of setting non-significant labels to NA or "" can cause plotting to take hours. Using NA for labels is faster but may conceal points, whereas "" avoids other labels and points but is slower. Using a continuous palette for a discrete variable (or vice versa) in binned plots will cause an error. When zooming into a specific chromosome, data thinning is turned off by default, which may result in a cluttered plot if thin.n is not manually adjusted.

workflows.name: standard_and_rescaled_manhattan_plot
workflows.intent: Preprocess and plot standard or rescaled Manhattan plots from GWAS summary statistics, with optional point highlighting and labeling.
input: gwas_results.csv (GWAS summary statistics containing chromosome, position, and p-value columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Format chromosome column as a factor ;; 2. Preprocess data using manhattan_data_preprocess() ;; 3. Generate the plot using manhattan_plot()
workflows.code:
simdata$chromosome <- factor(simdata$chromosome, c(1:22,"X"))
g <- manhattan_plot(x = simdata, pval.colname = "P.value", chr.colname = "chromosome", pos.colname = "position", plot.title = "Simulated P.Values", y.label = "P")
g <- manhattan_plot(x = simdata, pval.colname = "P.value", chr.colname = "chromosome", pos.colname = "position", plot.title = "Simulated P.Values - Significant", rescale = TRUE)
mpdata <- manhattan_data_preprocess(x = simdata, pval.colname = "P.value", chr.colname = "chromosome", pos.colname = "position")
g <- manhattan_plot(x = mpdata, label.colname = "label", plot.title = "Simulated P.Values with labels")
g <- manhattan_plot(x = mpdata, label.colname = "label2", label.font.size = 2, plot.title = "Simulated P.Values with labels", max.overlaps = Inf, force = 5)
tmp <- manhattan_data_preprocess(
  simdata, pval.colname = "P.value", chr.colname = "chromosome", pos.colname = "position",
  highlight.colname = "color", highlight.col = highlight_colormap
)
g <- manhattan_plot(tmp, plot.title = "Highlight Points", color.by.highlight = TRUE)
manhattan_plot(simdata, chromosome = 5, pval.colname = "P.value", chr.colname = "chromosome", pos.colname = "position")

workflows.name: binned_manhattan_plot
workflows.intent: Create a binned grid-based Manhattan plot for extremely large datasets to avoid plotting individual points, with custom bin summaries.
input: large_gwas_results.csv (Large-scale GWAS summary statistics containing chromosome, position, and p-value columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Preprocess binned data using binned_manhattan_preprocess() with custom summary expressions ;; 2. Plot the binned data using binned_manhattan_plot()
workflows.code:
binned_manhattan_plot(simdata, pval.colname = "P.value", chr.colname = "chromosome", pos.colname = "position")
binned_manhattan_plot(
  simdata, pval.colname = "P.value", chr.colname = "chromosome", pos.colname = "position", 
  bins.x = 7, # number of bins for the "widest" chromosome, either calculated by position or by number of variants
  bins.y = 100, # number of vertical bins
  show.legend = FALSE, plot.title = "Binned Manhattan Plot"
)
mpdat <- binned_manhattan_preprocess(
  simdata, pval.colname = "P.value", chr.colname = "chromosome", pos.colname = "position",
  bins.x = 7, bins.y = 100,
  chr.gap.scaling = 0.5, # scaling factor for chromo some gap
  show.message = FALSE # this suppresses some warning messages built into the function
)
binned_manhattan_plot(mpdat, bin.outline = TRUE)
mpdata <- binned_manhattan_preprocess(
  simdata, pval.colname = "P.value", chr.colname = "chromosome", pos.colname = "position",
  bins.x = 7, bins.y = 100, chr.gap.scaling = 0.5,
  # summary expression list
  summarise.expression.list = list(
    max_log10p ~ max(-log10(P.value)), # creates column "min_log10p", which holds the maximum -log10(P.value) among the variants inside the bin
    signif ~ ifelse(max(P.value) < 5e-8, "Significant", "Not Significant") # creates column "signif" which indicates significance of the bin
  )
)
binned_manhattan_plot(
  mpdata, bin.palette = "Polychrome::dark", bin.alpha = 1, bin.outline = TRUE,
  highlight.colname = "signif", signif.lwd = 0.5, plot.title = "Binned Manhattan Plot"
)

workflows.name: gds_variant_annotation_plotting
workflows.intent: Annotate GWAS summary statistics with gene/consequence information from a GDS file and plot the annotated Manhattan plot.
input: gwas_alleles.csv (GWAS summary statistics containing chromosome, position, reference, and alternate alleles)
workflows.stages: 1. Annotate variants using gds_annotate() ;; 2. Plot the annotated data using manhattan_plot()
workflows.code:
simdata_label$label <- gds_annotate(x = simdata_label, annot.method = "position", chr = "chromosome", pos = "position", ref = "Reference", alt = "Alternate")
manhattan_plot(simdata_label, outfn = NULL, pval.colname = "P.value", chr.colname = "chromosome", pos.colname = "position", label.colname = "label")
